response.content: {"findings":[{"location":"Paragraph 6","severity":"major","source_quote":"“I first felt the adjustment in my wallet, but I consoled myself that this was only temporary.”","suggested_fix":"Replace “nilijifichulia” with “nilijifariji” to convey that she reassured herself the change was temporary.","translation_quote":"“Nilianza kuhisi mabadiliko kwenye pochi zangu, lakini nilijifichulia kwamba hili lilikuwa la muda tu.”"},{"location":"Paragraph 7","severity":"major","source_quote":"“I am not mentally capable of handling one more duty.”","suggested_fix":"Use wording that conveys mental capacity, such as “Sina uwezo wa kiakili wa kushughulikia jukumu jingine.”","translation_quote":"“Sihisi nafsi kushughulikia jukumu jingine.”"},{"location":"Paragraph 8","severity":"major","source_quote":"“I became alarmed when I heard him yawning in the middle of the night and knew that he was not sleeping.”","suggested_fix":"Translate “yawning” as “kupiga miayo,” for example: “Nilishtuka nilipomsikia akipiga miayo katikati ya usiku na nikajua kwamba hakuwa akilala.”","translation_quote":"“Nilihisi wasiwasi niliposikia akinomeza katikati ya usiku na nikajua hajalala.”"},{"location":"Paragraph 10","severity":"major","source_quote":"“I felt like a lifeguard trying to keep a man from drowning while taking in a bit too much water myself.”","suggested_fix":"Render the image of the narrator herself taking on too much water, e.g. “Nilijihisi kama mwokoaji wa majini anayejaribu kumzuia mtu asizame huku nami nikimeza maji mengi kiasi.”","translation_quote":"“Nilijihisi kama mlinzi wa uzima akiijaribu kuzuia mtu asizame huku nikikula maji kidogo mwenyewe.”"},{"location":"Paragraph 11","severity":"major","source_quote":"“the victim can be misunderstood or misjudged”","suggested_fix":"Use a Kiswahili word for a person affected by hardship, such as “mhusika” or “aliyeathiriwa,” rather than wording that means the injured person.","translation_quote":"“majeruhi anaweza kuelezewa vibaya au kuhukumiwa kwa makosa.”"},{"location":"Paragraph 13","severity":"major","source_quote":"“Traumatic events in our plain circles tend to receive prayer, finances, and weekly budget updates.”","suggested_fix":"Translate “traumatic events” as events causing trauma or distress, not events causing physical injury; preserve “plain circles” as the source’s community context. For example: “Matukio ya kuhuzunisha katika jumuiya zetu za Plain kwa kawaida hupata maombi, msaada wa kifedha, na taarifa za bajeti za kila wiki.”","translation_quote":"“Matukio ya kusababisha jeraha katika mizunguko yetu ya kawaida huwa yanapokea sala, fedha, na sasisho za bajeti kila wiki.”"},{"location":"Paragraph 13","severity":"major","source_quote":"“Betrayal and rejection cause stress beyond measure.”","suggested_fix":"Translate “betrayal” as “usaliti,” not “uasi,” which means rebellion. For example: “Usaliti na kukataliwa husababisha msongo usio na kipimo.”","translation_quote":"“Uasi na kukataliwa husababisha msongo usio na kipimo.”"},{"location":"Paragraph 15","severity":"major","source_quote":"“Hearing yourself verbalize a stressful situation somehow clears brain fog and gives a clearer path forward.”","suggested_fix":"Correct the mistranslated verb “kunaoesha” and express that verbalizing the situation clears mental fog: “Kujisikia ukieleza kwa sauti hali yenye msongo kwa namna fulani huondoa ukungu wa akili na hutoa njia iliyo wazi zaidi ya kusonga mbele.”","translation_quote":"“Kujisikia ukisema kwa sauti hali yenye msongo kwa namna fulani kunaoesha ukungu wa akili na kunatoa njia wazi ya mbele.”"},{"location":"Paragraph 18","severity":"major","source_quote":"“Lingering stress can cause agitation, moodiness, and the desire to take control.”","suggested_fix":"Translate “agitation” as restlessness/agitation and “moodiness” as mood changes; “kusitasita” means hesitation and does not convey agitation. For example: “Msongo unaodumu unaweza kusababisha fadhaa, mabadiliko ya hisia, na tamaa ya kuchukua udhibiti.”","translation_quote":"“Msongo unaodumu unaweza kusababisha kusitasita, mhemko wa haraka, na tamaa ya kuchukua udhibiti.”"},{"location":"Paragraph 20","severity":"major","source_quote":"“Believe ‘Weeping may endure for a night, but joy cometh in the morning’ (Psalm 30:5).”","suggested_fix":"Translate the quoted Scripture faithfully into Kiswahili and localize the book name while retaining the reference number: “Amini, ‘Kilio huenda kikadumu usiku kucha, lakini furaha huja asubuhi’ (Zaburi 30:5).”","translation_quote":"Amini “Weeping may endure for a night, but joy cometh in the morning” (Psalm 30:5)."},{"location":"Paragraph 21","severity":"major","source_quote":"“God will make a way for you. Many times, He opens doors just when we are running out of options.”","suggested_fix":"Correct the changed assertion “Huona mlango ukifunguliwa” to say that God opens doors, e.g. “Mara nyingi, Yeye hufungua milango tunapokaribia kuishiwa na chaguo.”","translation_quote":"“Mungu atatengenezea njia kwako. Mara nyingi, Huona mlango ukifunguliwa wakati tunapokaribia kumalizika kwa chaguo.”"},{"location":"Paragraph 23","severity":"major","source_quote":"“And say with the Psalmist, ‘In thee, O LORD, do I put my trust: let me never be put to confusion’ (Psalm 71:1).”","suggested_fix":"Translate the quoted Scripture into Kiswahili and localize the book name, preserving the reference number: “Na useme pamoja na mtunga-zaburi, ‘Ninakutumaini Wewe, Ee BWANA; usiniache nichanganyikiwe kamwe’ (Zaburi 71:1).”","translation_quote":"“Na sema pamoja na Mwandishi wa Zaburi, ‘In thee, O LORD, do I put my trust: let me never be put to confusion’ (Psalm 71:1)."}],"passed":false,"score":62}
